title: Torsion cohomological dimension of a separably closed field
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field. Then
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq0$ in the sense of
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]: for every
torsion étale sheaf $F$ on
$\operatorname{Spec}K$ and every $q>0$ one has
$H^q(\operatorname{Spec}K,F)=0$.

proof.text: Let $F$ be any abelian sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}K$, not necessarily torsion. Take $K^{\rm sep}=K$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$. The group $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K/K)$ is trivial. Apply [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] to identify abelian etale sheaves with discrete $G$-modules, hence with abelian groups. The equivalence is additive by the cited statement, so it preserves kernels and cokernels (their universal properties), and is exact.

Apply [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] to the underlying sheaf of sets with $L=K$. It identifies $F(\operatorname{Spec}K)$ naturally with $F_{\bar s}^G=F_{\bar s}$. The map is restriction to a geometric germ, so it preserves addition and zero, and is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Thus global sections is naturally the additive equivalence of step 1, and is exact. No coefficient ring or uniform annihilator has been imposed.

source.place: Tag 04JM, Lemma lemma-global-sections-point, with L=K and G trivial

proof.text: Use the resolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. For a K-injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, exactness of global sections implies that the cycles and boundaries of $\Gamma(I^\bullet)$ are the sections of the cycles and boundaries of $I^\bullet$: kernels are preserved, and images are preserved as kernels of cokernels. Therefore $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(I^\bullet))=\Gamma(\mathcal H^q(I^\bullet))=0$ for $q>0$, since $I^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to $F$ in degree zero. In particular this holds for every locally torsion abelian sheaf, with no bound on its annihilators. By [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] this is $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq0$.
